outlook.statement: The current financial year (FY 2026–27) has begun to show early signs of recovery in the Optical Fibre Cable market. Global demand in Q1 2026 projected to rise by 6.8% year-on-year, reaching 136.70 million FKM; global production expected to grow by 7.2% year-on-year, surpassing 134.2 million FKM. North America leading with double-digit demand growth. Demand for G.657.A2 fibre exceptionally strong for drone connectivity, AI infrastructure, and advanced broadband. Several producers report fully booked order books for 2026. Emerging technologies like Hollow Core Fibre and Multicore Fibre progressing toward commercial deployment. Geopolitical tensions in Middle East pose risks of higher energy and freight costs, supply chain disruptions. Shortages in glass preforms, helium, and polymer feedstocks constraining production capacity.
Demand for Optical Fibre Cables has shown signs of revival since late March 2026 and is poised to strengthen in F.Y. 2026–27.
India's telecom sector is expected to sustain strong growth momentum in F.Y. 2026–27, driven by rapid 5G adoption, increasing fiberisation, and rising data consumption.
Global OFC business FY 2026–27 has begun on a strong note with both demand and pricing reaching record levels, likely to continue in near to medium term.
Indian wire and cable industry projected to grow at CAGR of 11–13% through FY 2029.
India telecom market projected to expand from USD 153.83 billion in 2025 to USD 193.34 billion by 2031, CAGR 3.88% between 2026 and 2031.
Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) set to cross 10 million subscriptions by end-2026.
BSNL's state-funded 4G rollout targeting 100,000 sites by March 2027.
B2B revenues projected to expand at CAGR of 4.29%.

The Board of Directors approved the Scheme of Amalgamation between the Company and Vindhya Telelinks Limited for the amalgamation of the Company into the Transferee Company w.e.f. the appointed date of 1st April, 2026. The proposed Scheme is subject to necessary statutory and regulatory approvals, including the approval of the jurisdictional Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).
The Group expect to contribute Rs 100.00 lakhs in defined benefit approved Gratuity plan during the financial year 2026-27.

The Company will continue to monitor the developments and may update the estimates as required in the period in which State(s) rules are notified and further clarifications/update on the governing provisions of the new Labour Codes are available.
Remote e-Voting period shall commence on July 31, 2026 at 9.00 A.M. and end on August 2, 2026 at 5.00 P.M.
